title: Reduce Supplements with Early Calibration Planning
summary: Identify calibration needs earlier with CCC ONE Calibration Guidelines. Improve repair planning, reduce supplements, and streamline workflows.
body_markdown:
Most shops do not need to be told that calibrations are becoming a bigger part of repair planning. The harder questions are how the required calibrations are identified and when are they identified in the process — and how much friction and inefficiency does it create when it shows up late in the process.


More than two thirds of estimates still don't include calibrations. And of those, less than half appear on the initial estimate. That means a large percentage of calibration work is being identified after the repair is already in production and repairs have started.


When that happens, processes start to break down and a supplement(s) is created. Although there are instances when identifying all the calibrations during repair planning is not possible, the less it happens once repairs begin, the better. Early identification of the required calibrations enables proper production planning and a more seamless communication plan and experience with the vehicle owner and insurance carrier. Plus, resources can be scheduled accordingly relieving cycle time pressure.


## Less Rework, Clearer Repair Planning


That is the opportunity Calibration Guidelines is designed to address: bringing calibration-related insight into the estimate before the repair plan starts moving downstream.


Available in CCC ONE, Calibration Guidelines lets shops pull diagnostic and calibration recommendations from connected providers while they are still building the preliminary estimate. That timing matters because the earlier calibration work is spotted during estimating, the easier it is to plan for it before the job is moved into production.


Instead of saving the estimate, sending information out, logging into another system, downloading a report, manually adding lines and pricing, and attaching a PDF back to the workfile, the shop can review recommendations in the flow of the estimate. From there, the estimator can decide which operations make sense to add, along with supporting notes and optional pricing.


The real value is not just fewer clicks. It is better visibility when it counts. Estimators can spot potential calibration needs earlier. Repair planners have a clearer reason and supporting documentation for the required calibrations. Technicians get better direction. And customer-facing teams have better repair insight to give owners about their vehicle. Clear documentation helps connect those decisions across the repair, so nothing gets lost between estimate, plan, repair, and customer conversation.


That visibility will only become more important as ADAS-equipped vehicles keep showing up in the bay. More cameras, sensors, radar, and related systems mean more repair plans will need to account for diagnostic and calibration work before the vehicle is ready to return to the road.


Calibration Guidelines is not meant to replace OEM procedures or a shop’s diagnostic partner. Instead, it brings relevant calibration documentation from the diagnostic partner closer to the estimate, helping shops support calibration decisions earlier and capture the relevant documentation for carriers to make reimbursement conversations easier.


Because the sooner calibration-related work is considered, the easier it is to build a cleaner estimate, reduce surprises, and keep the repair moving. In today’s repair environment, that is the difference between reacting to calibration needs later and planning for them from the start.
